messages:
marta: Heads up — starting a small RFC follow-up: cohort-aware slice retirement. Want to align on heuristics before I formalize the proposal. TL;DR: retire low-traffic slices in cohorts and amortize tech debt. Thoughts?

ryan: Sounds useful. What's the primary success metric here — ops reduction, lower p95, cost savings?

sasha: We also need to avoid cascading cold-starts when many slices go dark. Suggest ramped traffic redirection + automated warmup.

kevin: Agreed. We should use a small metric set: qps, p95, error-rate, and a cold-start spike signal. Also per-tenant affinity so we don't evict critical tenants.

marta: Proposed heuristic for initial cohort: slices with avg_qps < 10 AND 14d error_rate < 0.25% AND no scheduled cron jobs. Mark them as `gradual-retire`. Higher-risk ones go to `observe` first.

ryan: Can you show as a config example? makes it easier to implement in rollout tool.

marta: Sure — rough YAML idea:

```yaml
cohorts:
  - name: gradual-retire
    qps_threshold: 10
    window_days: 14
    max_error_pct: 0.25
    warmup_shards: 2
  - name: observe
    qps_threshold: 50
    window_days: 7
    action: monitor
  - name: immediate-risk
    error_pct: 1.0
    action: flag_for_manual_review
```

sasha: Add `min_tenant_affinity: 5` and a `burstiness_coeff` threshold to catch weekly/cron-y workloads. Otherwise we might retire something that bursts monthly.

kevin: Also include `min_recent_invocations: 5` so slices with only a couple of calls in the window don't oscillate. Edge-case: tiny tenants that are important for customers — we need an allowlist.

marta: Good points. I'll add `allowlist_tags` and `burstiness_metric` (7-day CoV) to the RFC. Plan is: compute cohorts daily, run canary retirements on a small batch, watch rollback delta for 72h, then proceed in waves.

arch-bot: RFC doc updated: https://redwood/team/arch/rfcs/cohort-retire-v2 (edited)

ryan: Operational note — keep billing tags intact when we retire or redirect slices so Finance can reconcile costs. Also capture pre/post token counts for cost analysis.

kevin: Edge-case: tenant that does large monthly syncs. We'll add a `scheduled_job_detection` signal (search for cron-like patterns and periodic spikes) and exclude those unless explicitly opted-in.

sasha: Can we add a tiny runbook snippet here for when retire causes errors? e.g. steps to rollback and rehydrate caches.

marta: Runbook line for the RFC draft: `step 1: /runbook retire-slice --slice $SLICE --cohort gradual-retire --dry-run`
`step 2: watch dashboard /dashboards/slice-retire (p95, errors, cold_starts)`
`step 3: rollback: /runbook restore-slice --slice $SLICE`

dev-bot: Scheduled job `compute_slice_cohorts` created, runs daily at 04:15 UTC — first run tomorrow.

ryan: I'll draft a follow-up PR to extend the rollout tool to accept cohort labels and warmup_shards. Assigning to myself for the tool changes.

marta: Assign to @ryan — thanks. I'll fold these edits into the RFC and bring to arch sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
